issues.main_description_html:
PRD #536 / design #537, task 3 of 5. Depends on task 1; pairs with task 2 (Map Mode).

Description

Per-building placement in Map Mode (PRD §UI3 + §FS5): move, rotate, and scale one selected building without affecting any other building.

  • Transforms are stored per building in canvasData and persist through save/reload.
  • Placement must not alter indoor geometry (walls/areas/points keep their local coordinates — the building transform is applied at render time).
  • Prior art: #525 floor alignment tools already implement per-floor transforms with Active/All Floors scope — reuse that transform pipeline (makeLevelPixelTransform in lib/map/geojson-utils.ts) rather than inventing a second one; a building transform composes over its levels' transforms.
  • Clear feedback while moving/rotating/scaling, and an explicit way to finish/exit placement (design reference #537).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Selected building can be moved, rotated, and scaled in Map Mode
  • Transforms save per building and survive save → reload
  • Other buildings and indoor room/wall shapes are untouched by one building's transform
  • Placement UI shows which building is being adjusted and how to exit placement
  • Unit tests: transform persists per building; transforming building A leaves building B's geometry byte-identical
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Merged via PR #553.

  • Building.mapTransform (LevelTransform shape, prior art #525) composes floor → building → project in makeLevelPixelTransform — single seam, all renderers covered, sibling buildings untouched. Inverse in lngLatToLevelPixel.
  • MapTransformControl "All floors" scope targets the selected building when buildings exist (label names the building); legacy no-buildings behavior unchanged. Active-floor nudge inverses the building frame too.
  • Pivot = building bbox center; persists in canvasData → autosave/undo/publish carry it.
  • Tests: src/lib/map/__tests__/buildingTransform.test.ts (isolation, default fallback, round-trip, regression). Suite 794 pass, lint + tsc clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #561: Map mode: drag-to-move shifts every building instead of the selected one (PRD #536 R13/R16)
issues.main_description_html:
PRD #536 validation gap 1 of 5 (R13 / R16). Highest severity of the five.

Description

src/lib/map/useBuildingDrag.ts was never updated for per-building placement (#548). Its Options type takes no building id, and the building-scope branch still writes the project-wide mapOffsetX / mapOffsetY (useBuildingDrag.ts:86-92), which makePixelRotator (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:107-127) applies to every building.

Consequences with 2+ buildings:

  • Drag-to-move (the primary move gesture, Map mode → "Drag building") shifts the whole project, not the selected building — R13 is only satisfied by the popup's small nudge arrows.
  • Dragging one building moves the others — direct R16 violation ("moving one building must not move other buildings").

Secondary defect in the same file: the floor-scope drag inverse (useBuildingDrag.ts:74-77) ignores the building's own mapTransform rotation/scale, unlike the nudge path which composes it correctly (src/components/editor/MapTransformControl.tsx:273-288). A floor drag on a rotated or scaled building therefore travels in the wrong direction/distance.

Fix direction

Route the drag's building branch through the same targetBuildingOf + patchBuildingTransform logic MapTransformControl uses, and compose the building frame into the floor-scope inverse. Fall back to the project-wide offset only when the project has no Building records (legacy).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Dragging in building scope moves only the selected building; sibling buildings are byte-identical
  • Legacy projects (no buildings) keep writing the project-wide offset — behavior unchanged
  • Floor-scope drag on a rotated/scaled building tracks the pointer correctly
  • Unit test: drag commit isolates the target building (rotate/scale isolation asserted too, not just translation)
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Description

deleteBuilding cascades only levels explicitly stamped with the deleted building's id (src/store/mapStore/buildingsSlice.ts:72 filters l.buildingId === id). Union the per-level bboxes projected through makeLevelPixelTransform (the same chain the geometry renders with) instead of projecting one global computeBBox through makePixelRotator.

issues.display_title: Issue #576: Empty building still renders a canvas instead of the no-floors placeholder
issues.main_description_html:
Reported while testing multi-building in the editor.

Description

Adding a building leaves it with no floors, so the Floor list correctly shows nothing — but the editor canvas keeps rendering a bare grid, which reads as a drawable floor that does not exist.

EditorCanvas.tsx gates the empty-project placeholder (design #304) on hasFloors(floorConfigs, canvasData), which is project-wide. With another building still holding floors it stays true, so the placeholder never appears for the empty building.

Nothing on that grid is actually drawable: FloorplanEditor already clears the model to __empty__ when no level is in scope (#536), and the engine's change handler returns early on a null active level. So every edit made there is silently dropped — the bug is that the canvas looks alive while it is not.

Fix direction

Gate the placeholder on the same building-scoped call the Floor list makes (buildFloorOptions), so the two cannot disagree. Placeholder markup stays exactly as designed in #304.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Adding a building shows the "No floors yet" placeholder from #304 on its empty canvas
  • Switching back to a building that has floors restores the canvas
  • A project with no buildings at all keeps its current empty-project behaviour
  • Unit test: a building with no levels of its own yields an empty floor list
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green
